newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Dexia CC listing raised 32 bln Bfrancs.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Dexia CC listing raised 32 bln Bfrancs.

text.p: The listing of shares in bank Dexia CC has earned Belgian towns and municipalities more than 32 billion Belgian francs toward cutting their debt in time for European economic and monetary union (EMU), parent company Holding Communal/Gemeentelijke Holding said on Monday.

"The various levels of power in the country have committed themselves to reaching the Maastricht debt norm as quickly as possible. To this end, the towns and municipalities have been invited...to use the proceeds of the bourse listing to repay debt," the Holding said in a statement.

More than 12 million shares in Dexia, formerly known as Credit Communal/Gemeentekrediet, were floated in November as part of a cross-border alliance with French bank Credit Local de France under which they took equal stakes in each others' operational units.
After the flotation Belgium's towns and municipalities still control around 65 percent of shares in Dexia's parent company, the Holding Communal/Gemeentelijke Holding.
The Holding said it would call an extraordinary meeting of the towns and municipalities for January 15, 1997, to vote on paying out the 32 billion francs as an exceptional dividend.
